extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent examiners, patent practitioners, policymakers (Congress), and patent stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Advisory recommendations and standards for improving patent examination quality, procedural guidance, fee policy, AI/tooling adoption, and efforts to expand inventor diversity and access to the patent system in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: More Like This Document (MLTD) AI search
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an AI search that finds documents similar to those examiners are studying by using title, abstract, claim(s), description, CPC, and examiner citation data to calculate similarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable Patent Examiners to perform MLTD searches to retrieve potentially relevant prior art; public demonstration previewed at PPAC meeting (Aug 2022). Link provided for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-augmented CPC auto-classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize AI to identify CPC symbols associated with claimed subject matter in utility applications to better identify claimed subject matter and route applications to the best-positioned examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO introduced CPC auto-classification in 2022 and is exploring additional applications where this auto-classification can be leveraged; see patent classification resources for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed PTAB feedback loop into quality systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Use each PTAB decision finding a claim unpatentable as an opportunity to understand and learn, embedding that feedback loop between PTAB and Patents into USPTO quality systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat PTAB outcomes as learning events to improve examination consistency and patent reliability/durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider non-obviousness context at institution phase for opportunistic copiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Study how objective considerations for non-obviousness in post-grant reviews of patents claiming products that provide a competitive advantage and have been copied can be considered more fulsomely at the institution phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO should consider whether to deny institution of these challenges to mitigate opportunistic copiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent updates to the MPEP and public training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to more frequent updates to the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and provide updated examiner training materials to the public between MPEP updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align information available to examiners and practitioners, particularly on case law updates, to positively impact quality of patent applications and examination. Last update was June 2020 (as of report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop guidance on discretionary denials via Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop additional guidance on discretionary denials, vetting such guidance through a Federal Register notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide public-facing vetted guidance so stakeholders understand discretionary-denial practices and criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable tools to improve design patent examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider tools (beyond hiring/training) to enable more efficient examination and grant of design patent applications, such as AI search capabilities and electronic publishing of granted design patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI search capabilities are available to utility examiners currently; consider making or creating comparable capabilities for design examiners to reduce pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage DOCX adoption without creating fee barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider additional ways (other than increased fees) to encourage public use of DOCX, using change management principles because fees introduce barriers for under-resourced inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fee-based incentives that may reduce access; use outreach/change management instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue stakeholder engagement and public solicitation of feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to engage with the public and solicit stakeholder feedback as part of the Agency’s role in advising on intellectual property policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC recommends ongoing public engagement and stakeholder solicitation to inform policy; use Federal Register requests for comments, meetings, and events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage Congress on IP issues and expand outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to engage with Congress on intellectual property issues and expand current approaches to reach stakeholders on policy matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC will provide input and serve as conduit for public feedback; keep congressional engagement active (legislation, hearings, responses to inquiries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and engage a national IP and innovation ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO with Commerce should define and engage a national IP and Innovation ecosystem to promote and increase access to STEM education, IP education, and increase diversity in inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on creating innovators through education, environments for commercialization, and expanded access to resources to bring underrepresented inventors into the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect demographic data to visualize inventorship (IDEA Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use patent data combined with demographic data to visualize participation in the innovation ecosystem and support passage of IDEA Act to enhance the Office’s ability to collect demographic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better demographic data will help identify underrepresentation and target initiatives to increase inclusion of women, veterans, people with disabilities, minority ethnicities, LGBTQ+, geographic areas, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and expand pro bono and law school clinic programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Support 21 regional Patent Pro Bono Program regions and the law school clinic certification program to provide pro bono legal assistance in patent and trademark matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet inventors where they are to reach veterans, lower socio-economic status individuals, those outside technology hubs, and those historically without access; infuse more funding and onboard more law-school clinics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an adequate operating reserve (OR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the operating reserve at a sufficient level—two to three months of expenses—to ensure USPTO financial wellbeing and resilience to unexpected financial changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OR funds placed into operating reserve upon congressional request for PTFRF funds; adequate OR helps weather continuing resolutions or appropriations lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee funding model: low entry fees subsidized by issue/maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a fee funding model where entry fees (filing, search, examination) are set below cost to encourage entry (small businesses/solo inventors), subsidized by issue and maintenance fees set above aggregate cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO recovers aggregate costs only after payment of later maintenance fees; PPAC endorses model because it promotes diversity, equity, and inclusion; sustainability depends on continued payment of issue and maintenance fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor filing/payment rates and detect patent filing fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently monitor rates of filings, payment of issue fees, and payment of maintenance fees to ensure sustainability; maintain robust procedures to identify anomalies and patent filing fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fraud examples include copied filings and improper micro entity certifications; USPTO has diligence procedures and should continue to identify and remedy filing fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify types and limits of fee-setting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize three types of statutory fee-setting authority (AIA broad authority, CPI-based adjustments, unit cost–based adjustments) and the USPTO’s reliance on AIA authority because CPI- and unit-cost authorities are insufficient for sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIA authority is time-limited (extended by SUCCESS Act to Sept 2026); PPAC urges Congress to continue/expand AIA authority and consider decoupling fee setting from entity size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek AIA fee-setting authority extension and decoupling by entity size
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend Congress grant permanent or extended AIA fee-setting authority, and expand authority to allow USPTO discretion to decouple fee setting from entity size so fee increases could apply differentially (e.g., only to large entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decoupling would help maintain sustainability while reducing barriers for small and micro entities; recommend permanent or another 7–8 year extension consistent with prior grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan periodic AIA fee-setting activities to maintain sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in AIA fee-setting activities periodically (USPTO expects to do so in next 2–3 years) to recover aggregate costs and maintain optimal OR in light of personnel pay increases and inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO can only set fees to recover aggregate costs (cannot turn a profit); planning helps avoid future fiscal stress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use previously collected but temporarily unavailable funds for patent quality and DEI
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine how previously collected but temporarily unavailable funds (e.g., Treasury-account balance ~ $1B and PTFRF balances) can be used to improve reliability/durability of patent rights and expand diversity/equity/inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once determined, request appropriation from Congress, identify specific purposes, and preferably seek appropriation outside normal budget scoring to avoid affecting other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand hiring/training to address examiner capacity (including design examiners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue efforts to hire and train more examiners (including design examiners) to reduce pendency and improve examination throughput.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine hiring/training with tooling (AI search, electronic publishing) to further improve efficiency and reduce backlog.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage international partnerships and dispute-resolution cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage internationally (e.g., WIPO GREEN partnership, MOU with WIPO on SEP dispute resolution) to improve access to green-technology platforms and to lend efficiency/effectiveness to SEP dispute resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperate on outreach, leverage WIPO Arbitration and Mediation Center resources, and engage stakeholders through joint programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public AI competitions and benchmarks to accelerate tool development
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor and use quantitatively benchmarked AI research competitions (e.g., U.S. Patent Phrase to Phrase Matching) using annotated USPTO Open Data to attract researchers and develop AI solutions for semantic understanding of patent language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitions can attract global talent, produce high-accuracy solutions, and inform future USPTO-led efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt cloud-smart strategies to modernize infrastructure and examination systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue a 'Cloud Smart Strategy' to reduce data-center footprint, improve resilience and energy use, and deliver best value while maintaining security; expand public cloud usage to improve systems like the Patent Examination Data System and Event Hub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cloud adoption improved stability, resilience, performance, image conversion, and reduced stabilization costs; increase public awareness through outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit public comments and hold events for stakeholder input (AI/ET Partnership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Federal Register requests for comments, meetings, events, and partnerships (e.g., AI/ET Partnership) to solicit stakeholder views and foster engagement across academia, small businesses, industry, other agencies, and civil society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design requests and events to reach the right audiences and prompt useful perspectives for policy development and implementation.
